text.p: Bonds closed firm along with Spain with the tone better in the shorter end than the longer where the 10-year cash lost some of its sparkle.
The negative spread with the Spanish 10-year cash narrowed to just under 10 basis points and was expected to remain around this level on Wednesday.
"The market is well supported...but the 10-year bonds, with some foreign sales, tightened the spreads (against Spain)," said one trader shortly before the close.
Traders said that despite a supply tightness, there had been an attempt to bring the spreads back to a more reasonable level.
But others said that by reducing the spread, the Portuguese 10-year bonds were well placed to follow Spain in the event of its gaining further.
The money market closed flat with the overnight unchanged at 7.00/7.05 percent.

The escudo is dependent on what happens on other crosses and in the dollar but traders said it looked likely to remain in a corridor between 101.00 and 101.35 to the mark this week. It ended European trade at 101.19/21.
